name: Lechweg Wanderweg
kurzbeschreibung: The Lechweg through the Tyrolean Außerfern: long-distance trekking along the wild Lech river, across the 200 m Holzgau suspension bridge, to the Lechfall in Füssen.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Lechweg is a renowned 125-kilometre long-distance trail honoured as Europe's inaugural "Leading Quality Trail – Best of Europe". From its mountain origins on the Arlberg, the route traces the unbridled course of the Lech – one of the last wild alpine river systems – through the pristine Nature Park Tyrolean Lech in the Außerfern region to the roaring Lechfall waterfall in Füssen, Bavaria. Connecting three regions and two nations, the journey treats hikers to dynamic gravel shoals, vast riparian forests, rare bird species, and picturesque Tyrolean villages featuring artistically painted farmhouses. This alpine river valley is among Central Europe's most biologically diverse habitats, offering multi-day walkers an authentic encounter with wild nature at its finest.

Route & Requirements

The entire trail is typically completed in six to eight moderate day stages measuring 12 to 20 kilometres each. The path follows well-marked riverside tracks, forest roads, and woodland trails without requiring technical mountaineering skills, though it calls for steady endurance and confident footing. The trail's greatest thrill is crossing the spectacular 200-metre-long Holzgau suspension bridge, hanging 110 metres above the dizzying Höhenbachtal gorge (an easy valley detour bypasses the bridge for those with vertigo). Sturdy hiking boots and waterproof apparel are essential. The trail is wonderful for active families with older children; only selected flat valley sections are wheelchair or pushchair accessible.

Visit & Arrival

Hiking is recommended from mid-May through late October. The trail is fully signposted with a distinctive white "L" against a blue backdrop. A key convenience is the Lechtaler hiker bus service (VVT line 110), running parallel to all stage locations to offer complete flexibility and luggage forwarding. Visitors driving to the Tyrolean Außerfern take the German A7 motorway to Reutte or cross the Fernpass (B179). Rail travellers can alight at Reutte in Tirol or Füssen station and transfer easily to regional bus connections.

Tips

Take time for a detour to the mysterious Doser Waterfall near Häselgehr, which emerges as if by magic each spring and vanishes completely by late autumn. In Weißenbach, visit the "Der Letzte Wilde" nature exhibition at the Burgenwelt Ehrenberg park centre, and utilise local guest cards for complimentary regional bus travel.
preis: Hiking trail and bridges free; luggage transport and local hiker buses bookable separately
oeffnungszeiten: Mid-May to late October (stages flexibly chosen)
